evidence: The sentence prints 'mean ± x' and cites Fig. 4. Methods p. 1514: 'All results are reported as mean ± SEM'; the same section says CMRglu data 'were not normally distributed' and were analysed with a gamma GLM, and the Fig. 4 legend says 'Values are median (minimum, maximum)'. The printed numbers are taken as mean ± SEM (dispersion_type = SEM). A by-eye reading of Fig. 4 (not digitised; approximate) shows a control whole-brain spread of roughly 7 to 23 µmol/min/100 g, which is incompatible with 3.6 being an SD for n = 6 (the minimum SD a range of ~16 allows is about 5.1) and at the edge of what an SEM allows (SEM 3.6 -> SD 8.8; the maximum SD for a range of ~16 is about 8.8). Read as SEM, the control values imply SDs of 6.9-12.7 µmol/min/100 g (CV 57-84%).
note: Interpretation, not a correction. Use SEM x sqrt(6) for an SD. Large control-group dispersion.
